title: The army takes the musicians; trombonist Frank Johnston
summary: The army, especially the tank corps with many Indian Canadians such as the Kahnawake trombonist Frank Johnston, was draining Rockhead's of players by 1942-43.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: So, everything is going on beautiful, beautiful, beautiful, then they start with going to the army and most of them was in the tank corps.
You see, most of Montgomery's tank corps was Indian Canadians and they had a trombone player, a boy name of Frank Johnston, I think. He was a Kawatina Indian.*
A Kawadna-- from La Prairie, that's outside of Montreal --
and he was a champ on the trombone, Frank was something else but Frank was always fighting people.
So, then, they had, I stayed there as I say, about until '42, '43, and I, Rockhead, the people, the army was taking up all the musicians. You look around, and he had his uniform on and he was gone.
